purpose: Original provenance and review metadata for supplied implementation references; not an ISO conformance declaration

sources.name: gql-compat

known_conflicts.issue: GROUP BY p.city conflicts with the included official grammar's binding-variable-reference grouping element
known_conflicts.disposition: Do not import as a normative positive; use an original alias-based case

known_conflicts.issue: Only the first WHEN operand matches, so the example does not detect an implementation ignoring subsequent operands
known_conflicts.disposition: Strengthen with later-operand, no-match, and null cases

known_conflicts.issue: Already-normalized ASCII does not distinguish normalization from an identity function
known_conflicts.disposition: Strengthen with decomposed/composed Unicode and all supported normalization forms

import_notes: The embedded official feature list has 228 entries; retain RDF4J's existing 2026 correction overlay and 234-entry target
Use YAML 1.2-compatible scalar resolution; stock PyYAML maps unquoted yes/no expected strings to booleans
Preserve exact numeric datatypes and graph identities in independent assertions
Keep generated syntax leads, reviewed semantic cases, vendor observations, and implementation-choice probes distinct
Keep absolute result and skip counts; conditional pass rates exclude skips and can rise if failures are skipped

known_conflicts.issue: An optional single comma allows at most two grouping elements instead of arbitrary repetition
known_conflicts.disposition: Do not replace the current grammar wholesale

known_conflicts.issue: Global case folding also affects radix prefixes; the newer OpenGQL grammar supplied in duckdb-gql explicitly makes 0x/0o/0b case-sensitive
known_conflicts.disposition: Use lower-case radix prefix spelling from the official BNF and newer grammar
